"""FeedEngagementConsumer — the #869 graph-driven cascade engine (epic #865).

Drains ``range.feed.exposure.>`` off the EXISTING ``EVENTS`` JetStream stream
(durable ``range-feed-engagement`` — binds, never creates; precedent:
``share_code_revoke``). Each message names SOURCE characters whose followers
are candidates to engage. The consumer:

    1. resolves ``org_id`` from the drainer-injected ``x-tenant-id`` header
       (the payload carries no org_id — see the drainer in events/outbox.py);
    2. traverses every source's followers in ONE bulk, weight-bounded BYPASSRLS
       drain read (``character_edges_by_characters`` — was N+1), keeping the
       strongest edge per follower;
    3. filters candidates to DRIVABLE synthetics (``is_synthetic`` AND
       ``assigned_user_id IS NULL``) via one bulk ``character_list_by_ids``;
    4. ranks by per-edge exposure score and caps at ``settings.MAX_FANOUT``;
    5. runs each candidate through the CascadeGuard gate pipeline in a SHORT
       claim tx (cooldown + budget); on Admit, makes a seeded, deterministic
       engagement decision; on a non-IGNORE action persists the interaction
       with cascade lineage (``cascade_id`` + ``hop_depth``), an audit twin, a
       per-member feed fan-out, AND re-emits a hop+1 exposure — those four in
       ONE SECOND short tx (Gate 6). Any REPLY/QUOTE LLM generation happens
       BETWEEN the two txs, with no pool tx open (finding #3). The re-emit IS
       the cascade.

TERMINATION. A cascade re-emits into the subject it consumes. Four independent
bounds — enforced by :class:`range_svc.cascade.guards.CascadeGuard` (hop
ceiling, per-character cooldown, per-cascade budget) plus the ``MAX_FANOUT``
width cap here — make every cascade finite, even seeded on a dense cyclic
graph. See ``tests/integration/test_feed_engagement_cascade_int.py``.

B2 persistence (per lane reconciliation): LIKE/REPOST decisions persist as
``range.post_interaction`` rows exactly as before; REPLY/QUOTE decisions
instead generate an in-character LLM body (persona-grounded prompt, mirroring
``ai_reply``/``event_reaction``) and persist a real ``range.post`` row —
``parent_post_id`` for REPLY, ``quoted_post_id`` for QUOTE — carrying the same
``cascade_id``/``hop_depth`` lineage columns (00059) as the interaction path.
The hop+1 re-emit anchors on the newly created post's id for REPLY/QUOTE (the
new post is what the next hop's candidates can now engage with); LIKE/REPOST
keeps anchoring on the engaging character, unchanged. The REPLY/QUOTE
``chat_completion`` runs OUTSIDE any pool tx (between the claim tx and the
persist tx — finding #3) so the cooldown/budget row locks are never held open
across LLM latency. A LLM rate-limit (``LLMRateLimited``) during content
generation naks the whole message with the server-advised delay
(``_nak_rate_limited``); because the claim tx has already committed, the
redelivery re-runs the guard and rejects that candidate on cooldown — the
engagement is dropped, never double-posted, and the cascade stays finite.

Gate 3 (RLS): the graph traversal + candidate/reach reads use the BYPASSRLS
``with_drain`` pool (org_id is known from the header but the reads span the
follow graph); every WRITE runs under ``with_org(org_id)`` so ``app.
current_org_id`` scopes it. Gate 6: interaction + audit + feed fan-out +
re-emit ride the same per-candidate tx — no direct ``publisher.publish``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
import uuid
from typing import Any, ClassVar

import structlog
from omnicore_prompt_safety import (
    GROUNDING_INSTRUCTION,
    SECURITY_DIRECTIVE,
    source_material_block,
    wrap_untrusted,
)

# Load the handlers package BEFORE range_svc.exposure.payload. payload.py
# imports range_svc.handlers._outbox at module scope, and handlers/__init__.py
# eagerly imports post.py, which imports back from exposure.payload — a
# pre-existing cycle that deadlocks ONLY when exposure.payload is the first
# module imported (e.g. a unit test importing this consumer in isolation).
# Importing _outbox first fully initializes the chain in the working order; the
# worker already loads handlers transitively, so this only hardens isolated
# imports. Must precede the exposure import below.
import range_svc.handlers._outbox  # noqa: F401 — import-order cycle break (see comment)
from range_svc.audit.emit import ActiveKeyProvider, emit_audit
from range_svc.cascade import metrics
from range_svc.cascade import settings as cfg
from range_svc.cascade.decision import Action, decide, seeded_rng
from range_svc.cascade.guards import Admit, CascadeGuard, Defer, Reject
from range_svc.exposure import payload as exposure
from range_svc.exposure.payload import ExposurePayload
from range_svc.exposure.scoring import INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT, exposure_score
from range_svc.graph.reinforce import graph_reinforce
from range_svc.llm import LLMRateLimited
from range_svc.repo import queries as q
from range_svc.workers.consumer_base import PullConsumer
from range_svc.workers.generation.completion_guard import sanitize_completion
from range_svc.workers.generation.event_reaction.persona import persona_system_preamble

_log = structlog.stdlib.get_logger("range_svc.workers.generation.feed_engagement")

_SERVICE_ACCOUNT = "range-svc-worker"
_TENANT_HEADER = "x-tenant-id"
_ENGAGE_AUDIT_ACTION = "range.post.cascade_engaged"
# Hard cap on a generated REPLY/QUOTE body — matches the event_reaction
# reaction-post convention (a cascade REPLY/QUOTE is a feed post, not an
# @mention reply, so it uses the 280 post cap rather than ai_reply's 200).
_MAX_ENGAGEMENT_BODY_LEN = 280

# Issue #2939. The USER turn's own label — a completion that echoes the turn
# back arrives carrying it, so ``sanitize_completion`` strips it from the head.
_USER_TURN_LABEL = "Post"

# A rejected completion is resampled rather than published or silently dropped
# (#2939). Same bound and rationale as ``event_reaction``: the observed failure
# was one bad sample from a working template, and the bound keeps a
# persistently-degenerate model to one extra LLM call per candidate.
_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS = 2

# Appended to the SYSTEM turn on a resample, so the retry cannot be a
# byte-identical replay against a greedy-pinned gateway. See
# ``event_reaction.consumer._RESAMPLE_DIRECTIVE``.
_RESAMPLE_DIRECTIVE = (
    " IMPORTANT: your previous attempt was rejected. Do NOT repeat, quote, or "
    "restate the post you are responding to, and do not emit any prompt "
    "markers or labels. Write ONLY the post text, in character."
)
_RESAMPLE_TEMPERATURE = 1.0

# LIKE/REPOST decisions map straight to a schema-backed interaction kind.
# REPLY/QUOTE are handled separately — see _generate_and_persist_reply.
_ACTION_TO_KIND: dict[Action, str] = {
    Action.LIKE: "like",
    Action.REPOST: "repost",
}

# Living Graph (epic #865 SP3): a non-IGNORE cascade decision maps to the
# INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT key ``graph_reinforce`` scores the edge with.
_ACTION_TO_INTERACTION_TYPE: dict[Action, str] = {
    Action.LIKE: "like",
    Action.REPOST: "repost",
    Action.REPLY: "reply",
    Action.QUOTE: "quote",
}


class _Deferred(Exception):
    """Internal: a guard Defer bubbles out to nak-with-delay the whole message."""

    def __init__(self, retry_after_ms: int) -> None:
        super().__init__("cascade guard deferred")
        self.retry_after_ms = retry_after_ms


class FeedEngagementConsumer(PullConsumer):
    """Pulls ``range.feed.exposure.>`` and drives + propagates the cascade.

    Constructor args (beyond ``publisher`` from ``PullConsumer``):
        pool:         ``range_svc.db.Pool`` — drainer sub-pool for the graph
                      traversal, app pool for the per-candidate write tx.
        llm:          ``StubLLM | LiteLLMClient`` — generates the in-character
                      body for REPLY/QUOTE engagements (B2).
        audit_keys:   HMAC key provider.
        rate_limiter: optional ``RateLimiter`` — when supplied, wired into the
                      CascadeGuard's AI-rate-token gate; ``None`` on the B1
                      no-LLM path (the DB guards alone govern termination).
        living_graph_enabled: Living Graph master gate (epic #865 Phase B). When
                      ``False`` (the default) the cascade is byte-identical to
                      the pre-Living-Graph engine — legacy reach read, seeded
                      deterministic decisions, the legacy 50.0 reach
                      half-saturation. When ``True`` the emergent model is live:
                      the reach read is decay-weighted (per-exercise half-life +
                      in-degree cap), each candidate decides against a FRESH
                      entropic RNG (not the seeded one), and the decision uses
                      the per-exercise ``reach_half_saturation``.
    """

    subject_filter: ClassVar[str] = "range.feed.exposure.>"
    durable_name: ClassVar[str] = "range-feed-engagement"
    max_deliver: ClassVar[int] = 5

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        publisher: Any,
        pool: Any,
        llm: Any,
        audit_keys: ActiveKeyProvider,
        rate_limiter: Any | None = None,
        living_graph_enabled: bool = False,
        retriever: Any | None = None,
        subject_filter: str | None = None,
        durable_name: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(publisher=publisher)
        self.pool = pool
        self.llm = llm
        self.audit_keys = audit_keys
        self.rate_limiter = rate_limiter
        self.living_graph_enabled = living_graph_enabled
        # #1476 AC3: baseline-article grounding for REPLY/QUOTE bodies. A plain
        # optional dep — ``None`` (the default) keeps every engagement
        # ungrounded, byte-identical to pre-#1476 behavior. Never raises; see
        # BaselineArticleRetriever.
        self.retriever = retriever
        self.guard = CascadeGuard(rate_limiter=rate_limiter)
        if subject_filter is not None:
            self.subject_filter = subject_filter  # type: ignore[misc]
        if durable_name is not None:
            self.durable_name = durable_name  # type: ignore[misc]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Message handling
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _handle(self, msg: Any) -> None:
        """Process one exposure message: traverse, decide, persist, re-emit."""
        log = _log.bind(subject=getattr(msg, "subject", "?"))
        parsed = self._parse(msg, log)
        if parsed is None:
            await msg.ack()
            return
        payload, org_id = parsed
        exercise_id = payload["exercise_id"]
        source_ids = payload["character_ids"]
        cascade_id = payload["cascade_id"]
        hop_depth = int(payload["hop_depth"])
        post_ids = payload["post_ids"]
        magnitude_hint = payload.get("magnitude_hint")
        log = log.bind(exercise_id=exercise_id, cascade_id=cascade_id, hop_depth=hop_depth)

        if not source_ids or not post_ids:
            log.debug("exposure has no sources/posts — acking")
            await msg.ack()
            return

        # Fire-time gate (Task 6d), ruling Q3c: gate on ``draft`` ONLY, never
        # ``paused`` — unlike every other consumer's ``execution_gated(...)``.
        # This hop IS the NATS message being declined: gating on paused would
        # permanently truncate an in-flight cascade, so a freshly-paused
        # exercise keeps generating for the seconds-to-minutes a live cascade
        # takes to drain. That is knowingly accepted here — "inert when
        # paused" holds at the fire boundary, not instantaneously.
        #
        # This consumer had no exercise row read before this change. Chose a
        # plain per-message ``q.exercise_get`` (no TTL cache): every hop
        # already performs several BYPASSRLS drain reads for the graph
        # traversal below, so one more PK lookup is not a new hot-path cost,
        # and a cache risks serving a stale "still draft" verdict across a
        # publish with no invalidation hook to correct it.
        async with self.pool.with_drain() as conn:
            exercise = await q.exercise_get(conn, exercise_id=exercise_id)
        if exercise is not None and exercise.status == "draft":
            await msg.ack()
            log.debug("exercise not executing — declining")
            return

        try:
            candidates, source_reach, settings, activity_map = await self._gather_candidates(
                exercise_id=exercise_id, source_ids=list(source_ids)
            )
            if not candidates:
                await msg.ack()
                return

            decay = settings.decay_factor
            # Living Graph: the decision saturates reach against the per-exercise
            # reach_half_saturation; flag OFF leaves ``decide`` on its legacy
            # 50.0 default (None → not overridden) so behavior is byte-identical.
            reach_half_saturation = (
                settings.reach_half_saturation if self.living_graph_enabled else None
            )
            engagement_hop = hop_depth + 1
            # A hop-0 exposure is the author's original post; every deeper hop
            # was reached via a repost-style amplification (see the B1 note in
            # the module docstring) — hence the interaction-type-weight the
            # propagation is scored with.
            itw = (
                INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT["post"]
                if hop_depth == 0
                else INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT["repost"]
            )

            metrics.observe_fanout(len(candidates))
            engaged = 0
            # #1476 AC3: lazy per-message grounding memo, keyed by post_id.
            # LOCAL to this ``_handle`` call — NEVER on ``self``, the consumer
            # instance is shared across messages. Every candidate on this hop
            # shares the same origin post and therefore the same FTS query, so
            # the first REPLY/QUOTE candidate that needs grounding populates
            # the entry and every later one on this hop reuses it. Lazy
            # because most candidates decide LIKE/REPOST/IGNORE and never
            # touch it at all.
            grounding_memo: dict[str, str] = {}
            for character, edge in candidates:
                did_engage = await self._process_candidate(
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    cascade_id=cascade_id,
                    engagement_hop=engagement_hop,
                    post_id=str(post_ids[0]),
                    character=character,
                    edge=edge,
                    source_reach=source_reach,
                    itw=itw,
                    decay=decay,
                    magnitude_hint=magnitude_hint,
                    reach_half_saturation=reach_half_saturation,
                    activity_map=activity_map,
                    grounding_memo=grounding_memo,
                    log=log,
                )
                if did_engage:
                    engaged += 1

            log.info("cascade hop processed", candidates=len(candidates), engaged=engaged)
            await msg.ack()

        except _Deferred as d:
            log.info("cascade deferred — naking with delay", retry_after_ms=d.retry_after_ms)
            await msg.nak(delay=d.retry_after_ms / 1000.0)
        except LLMRateLimited as exc:
            await self._nak_rate_limited(msg, exc, log)
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("feed_engagement_dropped — nacking for retry", err=str(exc))
            await msg.nak()

    def _parse(self, msg: Any, log: Any) -> tuple[ExposurePayload, str] | None:
        """Parse the envelope + resolve org_id from the x-tenant-id header.

        Returns ``None`` (caller acks + discards) on a malformed payload or a
        missing tenant header — the latter means the drainer contract was
        violated; we never GUESS an org.
        """
        try:
            payload: ExposurePayload = json.loads(msg.data)
            _ = payload["exercise_id"], payload["character_ids"], payload["cascade_id"]
            _ = payload["hop_depth"], payload["post_ids"]
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
            log.error("invalid exposure payload — acking", err=str(exc))
            return None

        headers = getattr(msg, "headers", None) or {}
        org_id = headers.get(_TENANT_HEADER)
        if not org_id:
            log.error("exposure missing x-tenant-id header — acking (drainer contract)")
            return None
        return payload, org_id

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Traversal + ranking (BYPASSRLS reads)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _gather_candidates(
        self, *, exercise_id: str, source_ids: list[str]
    ) -> tuple[list[tuple[Any, Any]], dict[str, Any], q.CascadeSettings, dict[str, int | None]]:
        """Return ``([(character, edge)], source_reach_map, cascade_settings,
        activity_map)``.

        Traverses each source's followers, keeps the strongest edge per
        follower, resolves drivable synthetics in one bulk read, ranks by
        per-edge exposure score, and caps at ``MAX_FANOUT``. All reads run on
        the BYPASSRLS drain pool.

        ``activity_map`` (node N4/N5, faction-activity-level-volume epic) is
        the raw ``character_id -> activity_level`` map from
        :func:`q.faction_activity_by_character_ids`, read in ONE extra bulk
        round-trip on this SAME connection (no second acquisition, no N+1 —
        mirrors the ``character_list_by_ids`` bulk read right above it). It is
        NOT defaulted here — a missing key and a stored ``None`` both mean
        "unknown activity" and the caller MUST resolve both through
        :func:`q.event_cadence_multiplier` via ``.get(character_id)``, never
        ``[character_id]``, so an unknown character reads as MODERATE cadence,
        never DORMANT's silent 0.0 (see that function's module comment).

        Living Graph (epic #865 Phase B): with the flag ON both the traversal
        and the reach read are decay-weighted against the per-exercise
        ``decay_half_life_seconds`` — the follower ranking uses each edge's
        lazily-decayed ``effective_weight`` and reach becomes emergent
        inbound-strength + leverage. With the flag OFF ``half_life`` is ``None``
        so every read is byte-identical to the pre-Living-Graph behavior (raw
        ``weight`` ranking, legacy ``count(*)`` reach).
        """
        best_edge: dict[str, Any] = {}
        async with self.pool.with_drain() as conn:
            settings = await q.cascade_settings_get(conn, exercise_id=exercise_id)
            half_life = settings.decay_half_life_seconds if self.living_graph_enabled else None
            # ONE bulk followers read across every source (was N+1: one
            # character_edges_by_character round-trip per source). The read is
            # bounded — ORDER BY <strength> DESC LIMIT MAX_FANOUT is pushed into
            # SQL so a celebrity hub with tens of thousands of followers never
            # streams its whole edge set into Python before we cap at
            # MAX_FANOUT. Dedup-by-follower below can only shrink the set, so
            # LIMIT MAX_FANOUT edges is always enough to fill the fan-out cap.
            edges = await q.character_edges_by_characters(
                conn,
                character_ids=source_ids,
                direction="followers",
                limit=cfg.MAX_FANOUT,
                half_life_seconds=half_life,
            )
            for edge in edges:
                follower = edge.follower_character_id
                current = best_edge.get(follower)
                if current is None or _edge_strength(edge) > _edge_strength(current):
                    best_edge[follower] = edge
            if self.living_graph_enabled:
                source_reach = await q.character_reach_bulk(
                    conn,
                    character_ids=source_ids,
                    half_life_seconds=half_life,
                    max_in_degree=settings.max_in_degree,
                )
            else:
                source_reach = await q.character_reach_bulk(conn, character_ids=source_ids)

            if not best_edge:
                return [], source_reach, settings, {}

            chars = await q.character_list_by_ids(conn, character_ids=list(best_edge))
            # ONE bulk activity-level read across every follower, on the SAME
            # drain connection (node N5) — raw stored ints/None, safe-defaulted
            # by the caller at the decide() call site, never here.
            activity_map = await q.faction_activity_by_character_ids(
                conn, character_ids=list(best_edge)
            )

        # Drivable = synthetic AND unassigned. A human-played or removed
        # follower is never AI-driven (mirrors the ai_reply stand-down rule).
        drivable = {
            c.id: c
            for c in chars
            if getattr(c, "is_synthetic", False) and getattr(c, "assigned_user_id", None) is None
        }
        ranked = sorted(
            ((drivable[cid], edge) for cid, edge in best_edge.items() if cid in drivable),
            key=lambda ce: exposure_score(
                _edge_strength(ce[1]), INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT["repost"], settings.decay_factor
            ),
            reverse=True,
        )
        return ranked[: cfg.MAX_FANOUT], source_reach, settings, activity_map

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Per-candidate: guard -> decide -> persist + re-emit (one tx, Gate 6)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _process_candidate(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        exercise_id: str,
        cascade_id: str,
        engagement_hop: int,
        post_id: str,
        character: Any,
        edge: Any,
        source_reach: dict[str, Any],
        itw: float,
        decay: float,
        magnitude_hint: str | None,
        reach_half_saturation: float | None,
        activity_map: dict[str, int | None],
        grounding_memo: dict[str, str],
        log: Any,
    ) -> bool:
        """Guard (short tx) -> decide -> LLM (NO tx) -> persist + re-emit (short tx).

        Returns True iff a non-IGNORE engagement was persisted. Raises
        :class:`_Deferred` on a guard Defer.

        Transaction shape (mirrors the sibling event_reaction / ai_reply
        consumers, #869 finding #3): the guard's cooldown-claim + budget-consume
        run in a SHORT tx that commits before any LLM work, so the cooldown-row
        lock + budget UPDATE are never held open across the (up to 180s)
        REPLY/QUOTE ``chat_completion``. The LLM body is generated with NO pool
        tx open, then a SECOND short tx persists the interaction/post + audit +
        feed fan-out + hop+1 re-emit atomically (Gate 6 — those four still ride
        one tx).

        Termination + idempotency are UNCHANGED as the single-winner arbiter is
        the cooldown claim's UNIQUE (cascade_id, character_id), which now
        commits in the first tx: a redelivery re-runs the guard and rejects on
        cooldown, so a candidate is driven at most once regardless of the
        tx split. A crash (or a mid-generation ``LLMRateLimited`` nak) AFTER
        the claim tx commits but BEFORE the persist tx runs simply drops that
        one engagement — the cooldown claim stands, so the redelivery finds it
        already-claimed and makes it a clean no-op. Nothing double-posts and
        the cascade stays finite (a dropped engagement re-emits nothing, which
        only shrinks the cascade). The Defer path still mutates ZERO cascade
        state (Gate 2 precedes the cooldown claim), so a deferred candidate
        re-drives cleanly on redelivery.
        """
        character_id = str(character.id)
        # --- Tx 1: guard claim (short — no LLM inside) ---
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            decision = await self.guard.admit(
                conn,
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                cascade_id=cascade_id,
                character_id=character_id,
                hop_depth=engagement_hop,
            )
        if isinstance(decision, Defer):
            metrics.incr_deferred()
            raise _Deferred(decision.retry_after_ms)
        if isinstance(decision, Reject):
            metrics.incr_rejected(decision.reason)
            return False
        assert isinstance(decision, Admit)

        # --- decide (Bernoulli(p) over an injected RNG, no DB / no tx) ---
        reach = source_reach.get(edge.followee_character_id)
        reach_score = reach.reach_score if reach is not None else 1.0
        # Living Graph: a FRESH entropic RNG per candidate makes engagement
        # genuinely stochastic; flag OFF keeps the seeded, deterministic RNG so
        # the cascade replays identically. At-most-once engagement holds either
        # way via the already-committed cooldown claim (tx1), NOT via decision
        # reproducibility — a redelivery is rejected on cooldown before decide()
        # ever runs. See decision.py's module docstring.
        rng = (
            random.Random()  # noqa: S311 — training-sim entropy, not crypto
            if self.living_graph_enabled
            else seeded_rng(cascade_id, character_id)
        )
        decide_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if reach_half_saturation is not None:
            decide_kwargs["reach_half_saturation"] = reach_half_saturation
        # Faction activity cadence (node N5, faction-activity-level-volume
        # epic): ``.get(character_id)`` — NEVER ``[character_id]`` — because a
        # missing key (unknown/soft-deleted character) and a stored ``None``
        # (no faction, or a NULL activity_level) are both "unknown activity"
        # and MUST resolve identically. ``event_cadence_multiplier`` maps both,
        # plus UNSPECIFIED/out-of-range, to MODERATE (1.0) — never DORMANT's
        # silent 0.0 — so a read gap here degrades a character to normal
        # cadence instead of quietly vanishing them from the cascade.
        faction_cadence = q.event_cadence_multiplier(activity_map.get(character_id))
        action = decide(
            edge=edge,
            reach=reach_score,
            itw=itw,
            decay=decay,
            hop_depth=engagement_hop,
            persona_stance=_persona_stance(character),
            magnitude_hint=magnitude_hint,
            rng=rng,
            faction_cadence=faction_cadence,
            **decide_kwargs,
        )
        if action is Action.IGNORE:
            metrics.incr_decision(action.value)
            return False

        # --- REPLY/QUOTE: generate the in-character body OUTSIDE any tx ---
        generated_body: str | None = None
        if action in (Action.REPLY, Action.QUOTE):
            generated_body = await self._generate_reply_body(
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                origin_post_id=post_id,
                character=character,
                action=action,
                grounding_memo=grounding_memo,
            )
            if generated_body is None:
                # Origin post vanished concurrently — nothing to reply to.
                # The guard claim already stands (cooldown/budget spent);
                # this candidate is simply a no-op engagement.
                return False

        # --- Tx 2: persist + audit + feed fan-out + re-emit (short, Gate 6) ---
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            audit_payload: dict[str, Any]
            if action in (Action.LIKE, Action.REPOST):
                kind = _ACTION_TO_KIND[action]
                await q.post_interaction_upsert(
                    conn,
                    post_id=post_id,
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    character_id=character_id,
                    kind=kind,
                    cascade_id=cascade_id,
                    hop_depth=engagement_hop,
                )
                target_post_id = post_id
                audit_payload = {
                    "post_id": post_id,
                    "character_id": character_id,
                    "cascade_id": cascade_id,
                    "hop_depth": engagement_hop,
                    "kind": kind,
                    "action": action.value,
                }
                # LIKE/REPOST re-anchor on the engaging character (unchanged
                # B1 mechanics) — no new post exists, so the SAME origin post
                # keeps propagating.
                reemit_post_ids = [post_id]
                reemit_anchor: str | None = None
            else:
                # REPLY / QUOTE (B2): persist the already-generated in-character
                # body as a range.post row carrying cascade lineage instead of a
                # repost interaction.
                new_post = await q.post_insert(
                    conn,
                    id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    character_id=character_id,
                    body=generated_body if generated_body is not None else "",
                    typology=None,
                    authored_by_user=None,
                    parent_post_id=post_id if action is Action.REPLY else None,
                    quoted_post_id=post_id if action is Action.QUOTE else None,
                    is_ai_generated=True,
                    cascade_id=cascade_id,
                    hop_depth=engagement_hop,
                    status="published",
                )
                target_post_id = new_post.id
                audit_payload = {
                    "post_id": new_post.id,
                    "parent_post_id": post_id,
                    "character_id": character_id,
                    "cascade_id": cascade_id,
                    "hop_depth": engagement_hop,
                    "action": action.value,
                }
                # REPLY/QUOTE re-anchor on the NEW post — it's what the next
                # hop's candidates can now engage with, not the origin post.
                reemit_post_ids = [new_post.id]
                reemit_anchor = new_post.id

            await emit_audit(
                conn,
                action=_ENGAGE_AUDIT_ACTION,
                target_type="post",
                target_id=target_post_id,
                payload=audit_payload,
                org_id=org_id,
                service_account=_SERVICE_ACCOUNT,
                request_id="",
                keys=self.audit_keys,
            )
            await q.outbox_fan_out_feed_updated(
                conn, exercise_id=exercise_id, org_id=org_id, post_id=target_post_id
            )
            await self._reemit(
                conn,
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                cascade_id=cascade_id,
                hop=engagement_hop,
                post_ids=reemit_post_ids,
                engaging_character_id=character_id,
                origin_anchor=reemit_anchor,
                magnitude_hint=magnitude_hint,
            )

            # Living Graph (epic #865 SP3): reinforce the engaging character's
            # edge toward the ORIGIN post's author, riding THIS engagement tx (no
            # new tx / no NATS / no audit twin). The followee is always the author
            # of ``post_id`` — the content actually engaged with — for every
            # action kind (a REPLY/QUOTE targets the origin post it replies to,
            # not the freshly persisted post). The author lookup is gated behind
            # the flag so a dark exercise stays byte-identical (no extra read).
            if self.living_graph_enabled:
                origin = await q.post_get(conn, post_id=post_id)
                if origin is not None:
                    await graph_reinforce(
                        conn,
                        enabled=True,
                        org_id=org_id,
                        exercise_id=exercise_id,
                        follower_character_id=character_id,
                        followee_character_id=origin.character_id,
                        interaction_type=_ACTION_TO_INTERACTION_TYPE[action],
                    )
        metrics.incr_decision(action.value)
        metrics.observe_hop_depth(engagement_hop)
        return True

    async def _generate_reply_body(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        exercise_id: str,
        origin_post_id: str,
        character: Any,
        action: Action,
        grounding_memo: dict[str, str],
    ) -> str | None:
        """Generate an in-character LLM REPLY/QUOTE body, OUTSIDE the write tx.

        Returns the (stripped, capped) body, or ``None`` if the origin post is
        gone (nothing left to reply to). Reads the origin post + faction in a
        short read tx, then calls ``self.llm.chat_completion`` with NO pool tx
        open so the (up to 180s) LLM latency never pins the cooldown/budget row
        locks (#869 finding #3). The caller persists the returned body in its
        own short write tx.

        Mirrors the persona-grounded prompt pattern shared by
        ``ai_reply``/``event_reaction`` (persona rendered as prose via
        ``render_persona_prose``, faction stance grounding, a hard character
        cap). ``self.llm.chat_completion`` may raise ``LLMRateLimited`` — it
        propagates to ``_handle``'s nak-with-delay handling; the cooldown claim
        already committed, so the redelivery is a clean no-op (see
        ``_process_candidate``).

        #1476 AC3: when ``self.retriever`` is set, grounds the prompt with
        baseline-article reference material. ``grounding_memo`` (keyed by
        ``origin_post_id``, local to the enclosing ``_handle`` call) makes
        every candidate on this hop share the one retrieval — the flags and
        FTS query (the origin post's body) are identical across all of them.
        Per the retriever's never-raises contract, no try/except wraps the
        call here.
        """
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            origin_post = await q.post_get(conn, post_id=origin_post_id)
            if origin_post is None:
                return None
            faction = None
            if character.faction_id:
                faction = await q.faction_get(conn, faction_id=character.faction_id)

        reference_material = ""
        if self.retriever is not None:
            if origin_post_id not in grounding_memo:
                grounding_memo[origin_post_id] = await self.retriever.retrieve(
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    query=origin_post.body,
                )
            reference_material = grounding_memo[origin_post_id]

        messages = _build_engagement_prompt(
            origin_post=origin_post,
            faction=faction if faction is not None else _FallbackFaction(character),
            character=character,
            action=action,
            reference_material=reference_material,
        )
        # #2939: guard the COMPLETION, not just its length. This prompt opens
        # with SECURITY_DIRECTIVE and untrusted-wraps the origin post, so the
        # model is taught the marker vocabulary — exactly the setup that had a
        # sibling consumer publish "<<<USER>>>...<<<END>>>" as a post body. A
        # rejected sample is resampled; ``None`` reaches the caller, which
        # already treats it as a clean no-op engagement.
        for attempt in range(1, _MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            if attempt == 1:
                raw: str = await self.llm.chat_completion(messages=messages)
            else:
                retry_messages = [dict(m) for m in messages]
                retry_messages[0]["content"] += _RESAMPLE_DIRECTIVE
                raw = await self.llm.chat_completion(
                    messages=retry_messages, temperature=_RESAMPLE_TEMPERATURE
                )
            body = sanitize_completion(
                raw,
                max_len=_MAX_ENGAGEMENT_BODY_LEN,
                labels=(_USER_TURN_LABEL,),
                echo_sources=(origin_post.body,),
                forbidden_fragments=(SECURITY_DIRECTIVE, GROUNDING_INSTRUCTION),
            )
            if body is not None:
                return body
            _log.warning(
                "engagement completion rejected (empty, JSON-like, prompt "
                "scaffolding, or an echo of the origin post)",
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                origin_post_id=origin_post_id,
                character_id=getattr(character, "id", None),
                attempt=attempt,
                max_attempts=_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS,
            )
        return None

    async def _reemit(
        self,
        conn: Any,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        exercise_id: str,
        cascade_id: str,
        hop: int,
        post_ids: list[str],
        engaging_character_id: str,
        origin_anchor: str | None = None,
        magnitude_hint: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Write the hop+1 exposure outbox row — the cascade continuation.

        The engaging character becomes the new source; the cascade_id is
        PRESERVED (never a fresh cascade — that is what keeps the whole cascade
        one lineage and one budget). ``origin_anchor`` is the Nats-Msg-Id
        anchor: LIKE/REPOST omit it (default ``None``), falling back to the
        engaging character — B1's unchanged mechanics, since no new post was
        created. REPLY/QUOTE pass the newly persisted post's id instead, since
        that post — not the origin post — is what the next hop's candidates
        engage with.
        """
        anchor = origin_anchor if origin_anchor is not None else engaging_character_id
        reemit = ExposurePayload(
            exercise_id=exercise_id,
            post_ids=list(post_ids),
            character_ids=[engaging_character_id],
            cascade_id=cascade_id,
            hop_depth=hop,
            origin_post_id=anchor,
        )
        # #1613: thread the reach-clamped magnitude FORWARD so deeper hops decide
        # with the same hint instead of degrading to neutral one hop in. None
        # omits the key (matching build_event_fire_payload's absent=neutral
        # contract), so a magnitude-less cascade re-emits byte-identically.
        if magnitude_hint:
            reemit["magnitude_hint"] = magnitude_hint
        await exposure.emit_exposure(
            conn,
            org_id=org_id,
            subject=f"range.feed.exposure.{exercise_id}",
            nats_msg_id=exposure.exposure_msg_id(
                cascade_id=cascade_id, hop_depth=hop, origin_post_id=anchor
            ),
            payload=reemit,
        )


def _build_engagement_prompt(
    *, origin_post: Any, faction: Any, character: Any, action: Action, reference_material: str = ""
) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Chat-completions messages for an in-character cascade REPLY/QUOTE.

    Mirrors ``event_reaction``'s persona-grounded pattern (persona rendered as
    prose via ``render_persona_prose``, faction stance grounding) — a cascade
    REPLY/QUOTE is a short reaction to the ORIGIN post's body, not a fresh
    persona post.

    ``reference_material`` is optional baseline-article grounding text (#1476
    AC3). Empty by default (byte-identical to the pre-grounding prompt); when
    non-empty it is appended to the USER turn only, labelled and
    untrusted-wrapped — never the system turn (decision 10, mirrors
    ``ai_reply.reply_prompt.build_reply_prompt``).
    """
    system = persona_system_preamble(faction=faction, character=character)
    verb = "reply to" if action is Action.REPLY else "quote-post referencing"
    system += (
        f"Write a short, in-character {verb} the post described "
        f"(max {_MAX_ENGAGEMENT_BODY_LEN} characters). "
        "Include one or two relevant, topical hashtags in most posts to match the platform's "
        "style — not every post needs them, and keep them natural and specific to the topic, "
        "not generic spam like #news. Do NOT include @mentions. "
        # Same JSON-envelope guard as event_reaction's prompt — see the note
        # there; ai_reply already carried this line.
        "Write ONLY the post text — no JSON, no metadata, no surrounding quotes. "
        f"{GROUNDING_INSTRUCTION}"
    )
    # origin_post.body is attacker-reachable — any participant can author the
    # post a cascade REPLY/QUOTE reacts to (issue #2419 / audit finding P1-18).
    user = f"Post: {wrap_untrusted(origin_post.body)}"
    if reference_material:
        user += f"\n\n{source_material_block(reference_material)}"
    return [
        {"role": "system", "content": system},
        {"role": "user", "content": user},
    ]


class _FallbackFaction:
    """Minimal faction-like object for characters without a faction assignment.

    Mirrors ``ai_reply.consumer._FallbackFaction`` — same shape, independent
    copy (no shared import) since each consumer owns its own prompt-building.
    """

    def __init__(self, character: Any) -> None:
        self.name = "Unknown Faction"
        self.description = ""
        self.stance_keywords: list[str] = []


def _edge_strength(edge: Any) -> float:
    """Ranking/dedup strength for an adjacency edge.

    Living Graph (epic #865 Phase B): prefer the lazily-decayed
    ``effective_weight`` when the read populated it (flag ON), so the candidate
    ranking follows CURRENT edge strength; fall back to the raw stored
    ``weight`` when it is ``None`` (flag OFF) — byte-identical to the
    pre-Living-Graph ranking.
    """
    eff = getattr(edge, "effective_weight", None)
    return float(eff) if eff is not None else float(edge.weight)


def _persona_stance(character: Any) -> str | None:
    """Derive a decision stance from a character's persona (``None`` = neutral).

    Reads a ``stance``/``alignment`` hint off the persona JSONB when present;
    an absent or non-dict persona yields ``None`` (the decision function then
    treats it as neutral).
    """
    persona = getattr(character, "persona", None)
    if isinstance(persona, dict):
        value = persona.get("stance") or persona.get("alignment")
        if isinstance(value, str):
            return value
    return None

       strongest edge per follower;
    3. filters candidates to DRIVABLE synthetics (``is_synthetic`` AND
       ``assigned_user_id IS NULL``) via one bulk ``character_list_by_ids``;
    4. ranks by per-edge exposure score and caps at ``settings.MAX_FANOUT``;
    5. runs each candidate through the CascadeGuard gate pipeline in a SHORT
       claim tx (cooldown + budget); on Admit, makes a seeded, deterministic
       engagement decision; on a non-IGNORE action persists the interaction
       with cascade lineage (``cascade_id`` + ``hop_depth``), an audit twin, a
       per-member feed fan-out, AND re-emits a hop+1 exposure — those four in
       ONE SECOND short tx (Gate 6). Any REPLY/QUOTE LLM generation happens
       BETWEEN the two txs, with no pool tx open (finding #3). The re-emit IS
       the cascade.

bounds — enforced by :class:`range_svc.cascade.guards.CascadeGuard` (hop
ceiling, per-character cooldown, per-cascade budget) plus the ``MAX_FANOUT``

        llm: Any,

        rate_limiter: Any | None = None,

        self.retriever = retriever
        self.guard = CascadeGuard(rate_limiter=rate_limiter)
        if subject_filter is not None:
            self.subject_filter = subject_filter  # type: ignore[misc]
        if durable_name is not None:
            self.durable_name = durable_name  # type: ignore[misc]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Message handling
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _handle(self, msg: Any) -> None:
        """Process one exposure message: traverse, decide, persist, re-emit."""
        log = _log.bind(subject=getattr(msg, "subject", "?"))
        parsed = self._parse(msg, log)
        if parsed is None:
            await msg.ack()
            return
        payload, org_id = parsed
        exercise_id = payload["exercise_id"]
        source_ids = payload["character_ids"]
        cascade_id = payload["cascade_id"]
        hop_depth = int(payload["hop_depth"])
        post_ids = payload["post_ids"]
        magnitude_hint = payload.get("magnitude_hint")
        log = log.bind(exercise_id=exercise_id, cascade_id=cascade_id, hop_depth=hop_depth)

        if not source_ids or not post_ids:
            log.debug("exposure has no sources/posts — acking")
            await msg.ack()
            return

        # Fire-time gate (Task 6d), ruling Q3c: gate on ``draft`` ONLY, never
        # ``paused`` — unlike every other consumer's ``execution_gated(...)``.
        # This hop IS the NATS message being declined: gating on paused would
        # permanently truncate an in-flight cascade, so a freshly-paused
        # exercise keeps generating for the seconds-to-minutes a live cascade
        # takes to drain. That is knowingly accepted here — "inert when
        # paused" holds at the fire boundary, not instantaneously.
        #
        # This consumer had no exercise row read before this change. Chose a
        # plain per-message ``q.exercise_get`` (no TTL cache): every hop
        # already performs several BYPASSRLS drain reads for the graph
        # traversal below, so one more PK lookup is not a new hot-path cost,
        # and a cache risks serving a stale "still draft" verdict across a
        # publish with no invalidation hook to correct it.
        async with self.pool.with_drain() as conn:
            exercise = await q.exercise_get(conn, exercise_id=exercise_id)
        if exercise is not None and exercise.status == "draft":
            await msg.ack()
            log.debug("exercise not executing — declining")
            return

        try:
            candidates, source_reach, settings, activity_map = await self._gather_candidates(
                exercise_id=exercise_id, source_ids=list(source_ids)
            )
            if not candidates:
                await msg.ack()
                return

            decay = settings.decay_factor
            # Living Graph: the decision saturates reach against the per-exercise
            # reach_half_saturation; flag OFF leaves ``decide`` on its legacy
            # 50.0 default (None → not overridden) so behavior is byte-identical.
            reach_half_saturation = (
                settings.reach_half_saturation if self.living_graph_enabled else None
            )
            engagement_hop = hop_depth + 1
            # A hop-0 exposure is the author's original post; every deeper hop
            # was reached via a repost-style amplification (see the B1 note in
            # the module docstring) — hence the interaction-type-weight the
            # propagation is scored with.
            itw = (
                INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT["post"]
                if hop_depth == 0
                else INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT["repost"]
            )

            metrics.observe_fanout(len(candidates))
            engaged = 0
            # #1476 AC3: lazy per-message grounding memo, keyed by post_id.
            # LOCAL to this ``_handle`` call — NEVER on ``self``, the consumer
            # instance is shared across messages. Every candidate on this hop
            # shares the same origin post and therefore the same FTS query, so
            # the first REPLY/QUOTE candidate that needs grounding populates
            # the entry and every later one on this hop reuses it. Lazy
            # because most candidates decide LIKE/REPOST/IGNORE and never
            # touch it at all.
            grounding_memo: dict[str, str] = {}
            for character, edge in candidates:
                did_engage = await self._process_candidate(
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    cascade_id=cascade_id,
                    engagement_hop=engagement_hop,
                    post_id=str(post_ids[0]),
                    character=character,
                    edge=edge,
                    source_reach=source_reach,
                    itw=itw,
                    decay=decay,
                    magnitude_hint=magnitude_hint,
                    reach_half_saturation=reach_half_saturation,
                    activity_map=activity_map,
                    grounding_memo=grounding_memo,
                    log=log,
                )
                if did_engage:
                    engaged += 1

            log.info("cascade hop processed", candidates=len(candidates), engaged=engaged)
            await msg.ack()

        except _Deferred as d:
            log.info("cascade deferred — naking with delay", retry_after_ms=d.retry_after_ms)
            await msg.nak(delay=d.retry_after_ms / 1000.0)
        except LLMRateLimited as exc:
            await self._nak_rate_limited(msg, exc, log)
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("feed_engagement_dropped — nacking for retry", err=str(exc))
            await msg.nak()

    def _parse(self, msg: Any, log: Any) -> tuple[ExposurePayload, str] | None:
        """Parse the envelope + resolve org_id from the x-tenant-id header.

        Returns ``None`` (caller acks + discards) on a malformed payload or a
        missing tenant header — the latter means the drainer contract was
        violated; we never GUESS an org.
        """
        try:
            payload: ExposurePayload = json.loads(msg.data)
            _ = payload["exercise_id"], payload["character_ids"], payload["cascade_id"]
            _ = payload["hop_depth"], payload["post_ids"]
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
            log.error("invalid exposure payload — acking", err=str(exc))
            return None

        headers = getattr(msg, "headers", None) or {}
        org_id = headers.get(_TENANT_HEADER)
        if not org_id:
            log.error("exposure missing x-tenant-id header — acking (drainer contract)")
            return None
        return payload, org_id

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Traversal + ranking (BYPASSRLS reads)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _gather_candidates(
        self, *, exercise_id: str, source_ids: list[str]
    ) -> tuple[list[tuple[Any, Any]], dict[str, Any], q.CascadeSettings, dict[str, int | None]]:
        """Return ``([(character, edge)], source_reach_map, cascade_settings,
        activity_map)``.

        Traverses each source's followers, keeps the strongest edge per
        follower, resolves drivable synthetics in one bulk read, ranks by
        per-edge exposure score, and caps at ``MAX_FANOUT``. All reads run on
        the BYPASSRLS drain pool.

        ``activity_map`` (node N4/N5, faction-activity-level-volume epic) is
        the raw ``character_id -> activity_level`` map from
        :func:`q.faction_activity_by_character_ids`, read in ONE extra bulk
        round-trip on this SAME connection (no second acquisition, no N+1 —
        mirrors the ``character_list_by_ids`` bulk read right above it). It is
        NOT defaulted here — a missing key and a stored ``None`` both mean
        "unknown activity" and the caller MUST resolve both through
        :func:`q.event_cadence_multiplier` via ``.get(character_id)``, never
        ``[character_id]``, so an unknown character reads as MODERATE cadence,
        never DORMANT's silent 0.0 (see that function's module comment).

        Living Graph (epic #865 Phase B): with the flag ON both the traversal
        and the reach read are decay-weighted against the per-exercise
        ``decay_half_life_seconds`` — the follower ranking uses each edge's
        lazily-decayed ``effective_weight`` and reach becomes emergent
        inbound-strength + leverage. With the flag OFF ``half_life`` is ``None``
        so every read is byte-identical to the pre-Living-Graph behavior (raw
        ``weight`` ranking, legacy ``count(*)`` reach).
        """
        best_edge: dict[str, Any] = {}
        async with self.pool.with_drain() as conn:
            settings = await q.cascade_settings_get(conn, exercise_id=exercise_id)
            half_life = settings.decay_half_life_seconds if self.living_graph_enabled else None
            # ONE bulk followers read across every source (was N+1: one
            # character_edges_by_character round-trip per source). The read is
            # bounded — ORDER BY <strength> DESC LIMIT MAX_FANOUT is pushed into
            # SQL so a celebrity hub with tens of thousands of followers never
            # streams its whole edge set into Python before we cap at
            # MAX_FANOUT. Dedup-by-follower below can only shrink the set, so
            # LIMIT MAX_FANOUT edges is always enough to fill the fan-out cap.
            edges = await q.character_edges_by_characters(
                conn,
                character_ids=source_ids,
                direction="followers",
                limit=cfg.MAX_FANOUT,
                half_life_seconds=half_life,
            )
            for edge in edges:
                follower = edge.follower_character_id
                current = best_edge.get(follower)
                if current is None or _edge_strength(edge) > _edge_strength(current):
                    best_edge[follower] = edge
            if self.living_graph_enabled:
                source_reach = await q.character_reach_bulk(
                    conn,
                    character_ids=source_ids,
                    half_life_seconds=half_life,
                    max_in_degree=settings.max_in_degree,
                )
            else:
                source_reach = await q.character_reach_bulk(conn, character_ids=source_ids)

            if not best_edge:
                return [], source_reach, settings, {}

            chars = await q.character_list_by_ids(conn, character_ids=list(best_edge))
            # ONE bulk activity-level read across every follower, on the SAME
            # drain connection (node N5) — raw stored ints/None, safe-defaulted
            # by the caller at the decide() call site, never here.
            activity_map = await q.faction_activity_by_character_ids(
                conn, character_ids=list(best_edge)
            )

        # Drivable = synthetic AND unassigned. A human-played or removed
        # follower is never AI-driven (mirrors the ai_reply stand-down rule).
        drivable = {
            c.id: c
            for c in chars
            if getattr(c, "is_synthetic", False) and getattr(c, "assigned_user_id", None) is None
        }
        ranked = sorted(
            ((drivable[cid], edge) for cid, edge in best_edge.items() if cid in drivable),
            key=lambda ce: exposure_score(
                _edge_strength(ce[1]), INTERACTION_TYPE_WEIGHT["repost"], settings.decay_factor
            ),
            reverse=True,
        )
        return ranked[: cfg.MAX_FANOUT], source_reach, settings, activity_map

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Per-candidate: guard -> decide -> persist + re-emit (one tx, Gate 6)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _process_candidate(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        exercise_id: str,
        cascade_id: str,
        engagement_hop: int,
        post_id: str,
        character: Any,
        edge: Any,
        source_reach: dict[str, Any],
        itw: float,
        decay: float,
        magnitude_hint: str | None,
        reach_half_saturation: float | None,
        activity_map: dict[str, int | None],
        grounding_memo: dict[str, str],
        log: Any,
    ) -> bool:
        """Guard (short tx) -> decide -> LLM (NO tx) -> persist + re-emit (short tx).

        Returns True iff a non-IGNORE engagement was persisted. Raises
        :class:`_Deferred` on a guard Defer.

        Transaction shape (mirrors the sibling event_reaction / ai_reply
        consumers, #869 finding #3): the guard's cooldown-claim + budget-consume
        run in a SHORT tx that commits before any LLM work, so the cooldown-row
        lock + budget UPDATE are never held open across the (up to 180s)
        REPLY/QUOTE ``chat_completion``. The LLM body is generated with NO pool
        tx open, then a SECOND short tx persists the interaction/post + audit +
        feed fan-out + hop+1 re-emit atomically (Gate 6 — those four still ride
        one tx).

        Termination + idempotency are UNCHANGED as the single-winner arbiter is
        the cooldown claim's UNIQUE (cascade_id, character_id), which now
        commits in the first tx: a redelivery re-runs the guard and rejects on
        cooldown, so a candidate is driven at most once regardless of the
        tx split. A crash (or a mid-generation ``LLMRateLimited`` nak) AFTER
        the claim tx commits but BEFORE the persist tx runs simply drops that
        one engagement — the cooldown claim stands, so the redelivery finds it
        already-claimed and makes it a clean no-op. Nothing double-posts and
        the cascade stays finite (a dropped engagement re-emits nothing, which
        only shrinks the cascade). The Defer path still mutates ZERO cascade
        state (Gate 2 precedes the cooldown claim), so a deferred candidate
        re-drives cleanly on redelivery.
        """
        character_id = str(character.id)
        # --- Tx 1: guard claim (short — no LLM inside) ---
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            decision = await self.guard.admit(
                conn,
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                cascade_id=cascade_id,
                character_id=character_id,
                hop_depth=engagement_hop,
            )
        if isinstance(decision, Defer):
            metrics.incr_deferred()
            raise _Deferred(decision.retry_after_ms)
        if isinstance(decision, Reject):
            metrics.incr_rejected(decision.reason)
            return False
        assert isinstance(decision, Admit)

        # --- decide (Bernoulli(p) over an injected RNG, no DB / no tx) ---
        reach = source_reach.get(edge.followee_character_id)
        reach_score = reach.reach_score if reach is not None else 1.0
        # Living Graph: a FRESH entropic RNG per candidate makes engagement
        # genuinely stochastic; flag OFF keeps the seeded, deterministic RNG so
        # the cascade replays identically. At-most-once engagement holds either
        # way via the already-committed cooldown claim (tx1), NOT via decision
        # reproducibility — a redelivery is rejected on cooldown before decide()
        # ever runs. See decision.py's module docstring.
        rng = (
            random.Random()  # noqa: S311 — training-sim entropy, not crypto
            if self.living_graph_enabled
            else seeded_rng(cascade_id, character_id)
        )
        decide_kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
        if reach_half_saturation is not None:
            decide_kwargs["reach_half_saturation"] = reach_half_saturation
        # Faction activity cadence (node N5, faction-activity-level-volume
        # epic): ``.get(character_id)`` — NEVER ``[character_id]`` — because a
        # missing key (unknown/soft-deleted character) and a stored ``None``
        # (no faction, or a NULL activity_level) are both "unknown activity"
        # and MUST resolve identically. ``event_cadence_multiplier`` maps both,
        # plus UNSPECIFIED/out-of-range, to MODERATE (1.0) — never DORMANT's
        # silent 0.0 — so a read gap here degrades a character to normal
        # cadence instead of quietly vanishing them from the cascade.
        faction_cadence = q.event_cadence_multiplier(activity_map.get(character_id))
        action = decide(
            edge=edge,
            reach=reach_score,
            itw=itw,
            decay=decay,
            hop_depth=engagement_hop,
            persona_stance=_persona_stance(character),
            magnitude_hint=magnitude_hint,
            rng=rng,
            faction_cadence=faction_cadence,
            **decide_kwargs,
        )
        if action is Action.IGNORE:
            metrics.incr_decision(action.value)
            return False

        # --- REPLY/QUOTE: generate the in-character body OUTSIDE any tx ---
        generated_body: str | None = None
        if action in (Action.REPLY, Action.QUOTE):
            generated_body = await self._generate_reply_body(
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                origin_post_id=post_id,
                character=character,
                action=action,
                grounding_memo=grounding_memo,
            )
            if generated_body is None:
                # Origin post vanished concurrently — nothing to reply to.
                # The guard claim already stands (cooldown/budget spent);
                # this candidate is simply a no-op engagement.
                return False

        # --- Tx 2: persist + audit + feed fan-out + re-emit (short, Gate 6) ---
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            audit_payload: dict[str, Any]
            if action in (Action.LIKE, Action.REPOST):
                kind = _ACTION_TO_KIND[action]
                await q.post_interaction_upsert(
                    conn,
                    post_id=post_id,
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    character_id=character_id,
                    kind=kind,
                    cascade_id=cascade_id,
                    hop_depth=engagement_hop,
                )
                target_post_id = post_id
                audit_payload = {
                    "post_id": post_id,
                    "character_id": character_id,
                    "cascade_id": cascade_id,
                    "hop_depth": engagement_hop,
                    "kind": kind,
                    "action": action.value,
                }
                # LIKE/REPOST re-anchor on the engaging character (unchanged
                # B1 mechanics) — no new post exists, so the SAME origin post
                # keeps propagating.
                reemit_post_ids = [post_id]
                reemit_anchor: str | None = None
            else:
                # REPLY / QUOTE (B2): persist the already-generated in-character
                # body as a range.post row carrying cascade lineage instead of a
                # repost interaction.
                new_post = await q.post_insert(
                    conn,
                    id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    character_id=character_id,
                    body=generated_body if generated_body is not None else "",
                    typology=None,
                    authored_by_user=None,
                    parent_post_id=post_id if action is Action.REPLY else None,
                    quoted_post_id=post_id if action is Action.QUOTE else None,
                    is_ai_generated=True,
                    cascade_id=cascade_id,
                    hop_depth=engagement_hop,
                    status="published",
                )
                target_post_id = new_post.id
                audit_payload = {
                    "post_id": new_post.id,
                    "parent_post_id": post_id,
                    "character_id": character_id,
                    "cascade_id": cascade_id,
                    "hop_depth": engagement_hop,
                    "action": action.value,
                }
                # REPLY/QUOTE re-anchor on the NEW post — it's what the next
                # hop's candidates can now engage with, not the origin post.
                reemit_post_ids = [new_post.id]
                reemit_anchor = new_post.id

            await emit_audit(
                conn,
                action=_ENGAGE_AUDIT_ACTION,
                target_type="post",
                target_id=target_post_id,
                payload=audit_payload,
                org_id=org_id,
                service_account=_SERVICE_ACCOUNT,
                request_id="",
                keys=self.audit_keys,
            )
            await q.outbox_fan_out_feed_updated(
                conn, exercise_id=exercise_id, org_id=org_id, post_id=target_post_id
            )
            await self._reemit(
                conn,
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                cascade_id=cascade_id,
                hop=engagement_hop,
                post_ids=reemit_post_ids,
                engaging_character_id=character_id,
                origin_anchor=reemit_anchor,
                magnitude_hint=magnitude_hint,
            )

            # Living Graph (epic #865 SP3): reinforce the engaging character's
            # edge toward the ORIGIN post's author, riding THIS engagement tx (no
            # new tx / no NATS / no audit twin). The followee is always the author
            # of ``post_id`` — the content actually engaged with — for every
            # action kind (a REPLY/QUOTE targets the origin post it replies to,
            # not the freshly persisted post). The author lookup is gated behind
            # the flag so a dark exercise stays byte-identical (no extra read).
            if self.living_graph_enabled:
                origin = await q.post_get(conn, post_id=post_id)
                if origin is not None:
                    await graph_reinforce(
                        conn,
                        enabled=True,
                        org_id=org_id,
                        exercise_id=exercise_id,
                        follower_character_id=character_id,
                        followee_character_id=origin.character_id,
                        interaction_type=_ACTION_TO_INTERACTION_TYPE[action],
                    )
        metrics.incr_decision(action.value)
        metrics.observe_hop_depth(engagement_hop)
        return True

    async def _generate_reply_body(
        self,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        exercise_id: str,
        origin_post_id: str,
        character: Any,
        action: Action,
        grounding_memo: dict[str, str],
    ) -> str | None:
        """Generate an in-character LLM REPLY/QUOTE body, OUTSIDE the write tx.

        Returns the (stripped, capped) body, or ``None`` if the origin post is
        gone (nothing left to reply to). Reads the origin post + faction in a
        short read tx, then calls ``self.llm.chat_completion`` with NO pool tx
        open so the (up to 180s) LLM latency never pins the cooldown/budget row
        locks (#869 finding #3). The caller persists the returned body in its
        own short write tx.

        Mirrors the persona-grounded prompt pattern shared by
        ``ai_reply``/``event_reaction`` (persona rendered as prose via
        ``render_persona_prose``, faction stance grounding, a hard character
        cap). ``self.llm.chat_completion`` may raise ``LLMRateLimited`` — it
        propagates to ``_handle``'s nak-with-delay handling; the cooldown claim
        already committed, so the redelivery is a clean no-op (see
        ``_process_candidate``).

        #1476 AC3: when ``self.retriever`` is set, grounds the prompt with
        baseline-article reference material. ``grounding_memo`` (keyed by
        ``origin_post_id``, local to the enclosing ``_handle`` call) makes
        every candidate on this hop share the one retrieval — the flags and
        FTS query (the origin post's body) are identical across all of them.
        Per the retriever's never-raises contract, no try/except wraps the
        call here.
        """
        async with self.pool.with_org(org_id) as conn:
            origin_post = await q.post_get(conn, post_id=origin_post_id)
            if origin_post is None:
                return None
            faction = None
            if character.faction_id:
                faction = await q.faction_get(conn, faction_id=character.faction_id)

        reference_material = ""
        if self.retriever is not None:
            if origin_post_id not in grounding_memo:
                grounding_memo[origin_post_id] = await self.retriever.retrieve(
                    org_id=org_id,
                    exercise_id=exercise_id,
                    query=origin_post.body,
                )
            reference_material = grounding_memo[origin_post_id]

        messages = _build_engagement_prompt(
            origin_post=origin_post,
            faction=faction if faction is not None else _FallbackFaction(character),
            character=character,
            action=action,
            reference_material=reference_material,
        )
        # #2939: guard the COMPLETION, not just its length. This prompt opens
        # with SECURITY_DIRECTIVE and untrusted-wraps the origin post, so the
        # model is taught the marker vocabulary — exactly the setup that had a
        # sibling consumer publish "<<<USER>>>...<<<END>>>" as a post body. A
        # rejected sample is resampled; ``None`` reaches the caller, which
        # already treats it as a clean no-op engagement.
        for attempt in range(1, _MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            if attempt == 1:
                raw: str = await self.llm.chat_completion(messages=messages)
            else:
                retry_messages = [dict(m) for m in messages]
                retry_messages[0]["content"] += _RESAMPLE_DIRECTIVE
                raw = await self.llm.chat_completion(
                    messages=retry_messages, temperature=_RESAMPLE_TEMPERATURE
                )
            body = sanitize_completion(
                raw,
                max_len=_MAX_ENGAGEMENT_BODY_LEN,
                labels=(_USER_TURN_LABEL,),
                echo_sources=(origin_post.body,),
                forbidden_fragments=(SECURITY_DIRECTIVE, GROUNDING_INSTRUCTION),
            )
            if body is not None:
                return body
            _log.warning(
                "engagement completion rejected (empty, JSON-like, prompt "
                "scaffolding, or an echo of the origin post)",
                org_id=org_id,
                exercise_id=exercise_id,
                origin_post_id=origin_post_id,
                character_id=getattr(character, "id", None),
                attempt=attempt,
                max_attempts=_MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS,
            )
        return None

    async def _reemit(
        self,
        conn: Any,
        *,
        org_id: str,
        exercise_id: str,
        cascade_id: str,
        hop: int,
        post_ids: list[str],
        engaging_character_id: str,
        origin_anchor: str | None = None,
        magnitude_hint: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Write the hop+1 exposure outbox row — the cascade continuation.

        The engaging character becomes the new source; the cascade_id is
        PRESERVED (never a fresh cascade — that is what keeps the whole cascade
        one lineage and one budget). ``origin_anchor`` is the Nats-Msg-Id
        anchor: LIKE/REPOST omit it (default ``None``), falling back to the
        engaging character — B1's unchanged mechanics, since no new post was
        created. REPLY/QUOTE pass the newly persisted post's id instead, since
        that post — not the origin post — is what the next hop's candidates
        engage with.
        """
        anchor = origin_anchor if origin_anchor is not None else engaging_character_id
        reemit = ExposurePayload(
            exercise_id=exercise_id,
            post_ids=list(post_ids),
            character_ids=[engaging_character_id],
            cascade_id=cascade_id,
            hop_depth=hop,
            origin_post_id=anchor,
        )
        # #1613: thread the reach-clamped magnitude FORWARD so deeper hops decide
        # with the same hint instead of degrading to neutral one hop in. None
        # omits the key (matching build_event_fire_payload's absent=neutral
        # contract), so a magnitude-less cascade re-emits byte-identically.
        if magnitude_hint:

If you want to:

- **Regenerate proto stubs (Go/Python/TS)**: `make proto`
- **Regenerate only TS proto stubs**: `make proto-ts`
- **Lint proto**: `make proto-lint`
- **Check proto breaking changes**: `make proto-breaking`
- **Run Go tests for a service**: `cd services/<svc> && go test -short ./...` (or `make <svc>-test`)
- **Run one Go test by name**: `go test -run '^TestName$' ./internal/...`
- **Run Go integration tests**: `go test -tags=integration -run '^TestName$' ./tests/integration/...` (or `make <svc>-test-int`, Docker required)
- **Run all Go modules + coverage file**: `make go-test` (or `make go-test-short` to skip testcontainers)
- **Check Go coverage gate**: `make go-coverage`
- **Tidy Go modules**: `make go-tidy`
- **Vet Go code**: `go vet ./...` (from service dir)
- **Run Vitest for one workspace**: `pnpm test`
- **Watch Vitest (TDD loop)**: `pnpm test:watch`
- **Run one Vitest test by name**: `pnpm test -- --run -t "<name>"`
- **Run Vitest with coverage**: `pnpm test -- --coverage`
- **Recompile Paraglide i18n messages**: `pnpm --filter @omnicore-platform/platform-chrome run compile-messages` (then hand-wire `frontends/platform-chrome/src/paraglide/messages.ts`)
- **Audit i18n locale parity/ICU/glossary**: `npx tsx scripts/i18n-audit.ts`
- **Fast glossary-only i18n check**: `cd frontends/platform-chrome && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/glossary.regression.test.ts`
- **Regenerate Range location-wizard geo shards (offline)**: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts` (network refresh: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts --fetch` first, to repopulate `scripts/geo-sources/`)
- **Lint an MFE**: `pnpm lint`
- **Typecheck an MFE**: `pnpm typecheck`
- **Bring up the whole stack (baked images)**: `make up` (`SCOPE=<vertical>` to limit, `CLEAN=1` to wipe volumes, `BUILD=1` to rebuild images from fresh proto)
- **`make up` never builds two MFE images at once — not even the ones `BUILD=` did not name**: each Vite build takes an 8GB Node heap, so the guarded loop (`_build-guarded`) builds non-MFE images in parallel and MFE images strictly one at a time. That guard used to cover only the `BUILD=`-selected set, while `up`'s final `docker compose up -d` carried no `--no-build` and every locally-built service keeps its `build:` context — so anything `BUILD=` missed and `stack-pin-images.py` could not snapshot (which is *everything* on a machine with no bare `:dev` tags left to snapshot from) was built by **compose** instead, all at once. 11 concurrent Vite builds either die with `ResourceExhausted: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm run build" ... cannot allocate memory` or drives an OOM-kill spiral that wedges the Docker daemon, so `make up` just *hangs* with no error at all. `up` now plans the absent set itself (`platform/scripts/plan-implicit-builds.py`), builds it through the same guard, and passes `--no-build` so any remaining hole fails loudly instead of fanning out. `make dev` deliberately keeps compose's implicit build: its MFE layer is host-side vite servers, not containers, so only service images can be built there. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_build_guarded.py platform/scripts/test_plan_implicit_builds.py -q`.

Without this, two worktrees would resolve the same compose project and the second `make up` would recreate the first's containers from its own source, i.e. a reviewer's stack silently serving another branch's code. Pick a different name (`make up STACK=<name>-2`) or release it with `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py release <name>`.

The GPU can't be meaningfully partitioned, so a real shared instance is future work; until then, budget ~792 MiB/stack for it specifically, on top of the capacity figures below.
- **Local stack capacity**: one walled stack is ~76 containers behind one published port, ~50-80s to boot. Four stacks running concurrently (305 containers) measured 8.23 GiB of a 23.43 GiB Docker Desktop VM (35%) once idle — idle stacks compress well below their boot-time peak, so the ~4.2 GiB/stack figure in the design spec (measured immediately post-boot) overstates steady state.
- **EVERY locally-built image is tagged per stack, not just shell-mfe**: a walled stack runs `omnicore-platform/<svc>:<tag>-<name>` (e.g. `range-svc:dev-review`, and `:dev-hotreload-review` under `make dev`); shell-mfe keeps its own `:walled-<name>`. Before this, the compose project, hostname, port, mTLS tree and litellm keys were all per-stack but the ~67 `image: ...:dev` tags were machine-global, so ANY worktree's `make up STACK=<x> BUILD=...` replaced the image a different, still-running stack would resolve on its next container recreate — that stack then silently served another branch's code, and all 11 isolation vectors still passed because every one of them tested *runtime* isolation. `up`/`dev` now snapshot the tags via `docker tag` (metadata only, no rebuild) just before `up -d`; see `platform/scripts/stack-pin-images.py`.
- **A pinned stack does NOT pick up a newer `:dev` on restart — that's the point**: the snapshot is sticky, so a plain `make up STACK=<name>` keeps serving the image IDs it was pinned to even after another worktree rebuilds `:dev`. To deliberately adopt the current build, pass `REPIN=1` (`make up STACK=<name> REPIN=1`). A `BUILD=` run always builds straight into the per-stack tag, so it needs no `REPIN`.
- **Vector 12 is image provenance**: it fails a stack whose containers sit on a machine-global (unsuffixed) tag, and separately flags a container whose running image ID no longer matches what its own tag resolves to — i.e. the tag was rebuilt underneath a live container. The unwalled `platform` stack is SKIPPED there, since it legitimately owns the bare `:dev` tags.
